title: 🍂 A Fall Reminder About Recycling & Windy Weather 🍂
bodyHtml:
🍂 A Fall Reminder About Recycling & Windy Weather 🍂
With fall here, we’re also entering the season of higher winds and stronger gusts. A quick reminder that putting recycling out too early can sometimes create a problem for our neighbors - literally.
When recycling containers, cardboard, and other lightweight materials are left outside overnight or for an extended period, a strong gust can send items blowing into neighboring yards, streets, or other areas. Unfortunately, once those items travel, someone else may be left to clean them up - something that can often be prevented with a little extra planning.
A few things to consider on windy days:
♻️ Check the forecast before putting recycling out. Pay particular attention to predicted wind gusts, not just the average wind speed. If gusts are expected to reach around 15 mph or higher for loose paper or 20-25 mph for other loose objects, it may be a good indication to take extra precautions.
♻️ Avoid putting recycling out the day before when possible. The longer lightweight materials are outside, the more opportunity there is for them to become airborne.
♻️ Consider using a lid or securing your recycling container when windy conditions are expected. Make sure anything used to secure a container is safe and it won’t become a hazard.
♻️ Make sure cardboard and other loose materials are contained rather than left where they can easily catch the wind.
A little attention to the weather forecast can go a long way toward keeping our neighborhood clean and preventing someone else from having to chase down recycling that originated somewhere else.
Thanks, everyone, for helping keep our community clean and for looking out for our neighbors! 🍁♻️
